log.text: Welcome to the magnet test table at the void deck! Today we find out what a magnet is, and which materials it really pulls. Remember: test, do not guess!
A magnet, a steel pin and a copper wire. Both are metal. Which one will the magnet pull?
Locked in!
Let's see what the buddies picked.
Correct!
The magnet pulled the steel pin across the gap, but the copper wire did not move at all. Being light is not the reason.
I tested Mum's iron wok. The magnet could not lift it, so the wok is not attracted to the magnet!
Is Momo right? If something is not right, tap HOLD ON!
Good catch! What is wrong with it?
Correct!
Oops! You caught me!
When I let go, the magnet holds on to the side of the wok. The wok is attracted. It is just too heavy to lift!
Two rinsed cans, both metal. Which can will the magnet pull? The drink can, the food tin, or both?
Locked in!
Let's see what the buddies picked.
Correct!
The steel food tin is pulled. Drink cans like this are made of aluminium, and aluminium is not iron or steel, so the magnet ignores it.
Showdown! Double points. Tap the wrong line in Basil's homework.
You found it! Double points!
The aluminium foil is not attracted to the magnet, so it is made of a non-magnetic material.
We cannot tell by looking. The magnet did not attract the foil, so the foil is non-magnetic.
Bring Basil's magnet near each object on the test table. Is it made of a magnetic material, or a non-magnetic material?
Mission complete!
Let's count your points on the score hand!
A perfect game! High five!
High five!
High five!
High five!
Level complete! Well done.
Fun fact!
Deep in the sea lives a snail with iron in its shell. A magnet can attract this snail!
